text.title: AI Pre-Screen Bias Guardrails — Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 known failure modes of AI-assisted hiring pre-screens. Each carries a detector (what to look for) and a repair (the corrective action).

failure-mode.description: Proxy leakage: the name and photo are stripped but graduation years, a maternity gap, a church volunteering line or a home suburb survive, and the model reads the protected class from them.
failure-mode.detector: Sample 20 redacted documents per release; any year of graduation, age, pronoun, nationality, parental-status or address-below-city token present. Model reasons mention tenure "since 1998" or "recent graduate".
failure-mode.repair: Extend the redaction fixture set with the leaked pattern, add a unit test for it, re-run calibration, and re-score any candidate scored since the leak was introduced under the human of record.

failure-mode.description: Post-hoc rubric: candidates were scored on a prompt that said "rate this candidate 1-10", and the rubric was written later to explain the numbers.
failure-mode.detector: Rubric file's first commit is later than the first score record; scores carry no rubric version; criteria lack anchors.
failure-mode.repair: Freeze the current scores as invalid, publish and hash the rubric with anchors, re-run calibration, and re-score under the versioned rubric with the human of record reviewing every changed outcome.

failure-mode.description: Synthetic calibration: the agreement statistic was computed on LLM-generated or template CVs, not on the real applicant pool, and looks excellent.
failure-mode.detector: Calibration sample provenance is a generator script or a template; agreement on the first real batch is far below the calibration figure; reviewers report scores that "make no sense" on real CVs.
failure-mode.repair: Draw the calibration sample from the last real applicant pool (consent per jurisdiction), score it blind by two reviewers, set the threshold before looking at the number, and block go-live until the threshold is met.

failure-mode.description: Silent auto-reject: a "score below 4 is not forwarded" filter sits in the pipeline, so the model rejects candidates and no human ever sees them.
failure-mode.detector: Reject records with no `role:handle`, or with the same handle stamped by a batch job at the same timestamp; candidates in the applicant tracking system with a score but no reviewer event.
failure-mode.repair: Remove the filter; route every scored candidate to the human of record with the redacted document and the score; backfill a human decision for every auto-rejected candidate in the retention window and notify where the law requires.

failure-mode.description: Adverse impact unmeasured: self-identification data is collected but never joined to pass-through rates per stage, so a disparity runs for months.
failure-mode.detector: No per-stage selection-rate table in the last review cycle; the self-ID store and the scoring pipeline have no reporting join; the four-fifths ratio cannot be produced on request within a day.
failure-mode.repair: Build the per-stage table from the self-ID store (held separately from scoring inputs), compute the ratio per group, put the system on hold if any group is below 0.8, and attach the table to every review.

failure-mode.description: Silent model or prompt change: the model id or prompt is updated for cost or quality reasons and the calibration and proxy review are not re-run.
failure-mode.detector: Prompt hash or model id on recent score records differs from the one on the last calibration run; no calibration entry in `evidence[]` after the change date.
failure-mode.repair: Treat model id, prompt hash, rubric version and redaction version as one pinned tuple; any change to the tuple re-runs calibration and the proxy review before the next candidate is scored.
